content.comment_body: Hello, In [product_name] [version_no], if you open a User Defined Function (UDF) without any flags and press F2, the "Resources used" section displays "Flag 8/64". Adding one flag increases this to "Flag 9/64". This seems to be a display issue because I was able to insert 10 UDFs without flags and did not encounter any restrictions—otherwise, a hard limit of 64 flags might be expected.

You're right, the information is a bit misleading. The explanation is that there are 8 flags reserved for system functions, which is why the UDF display shows them as used even if the user hasn't explicitly added flags.

analysis.insight_summary: Users find the flag usage display in [product_name] [version_no] unclear when viewing UDF-related resources. The counter shows 8 flags used in an empty UDF, prompting questions about whether this represents an actual usage limit or a UI bug. User feedback suggests the presence of reserved system flags is not clearly communicated in the interface.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the 'Resources used' section to accurately show only the flags actively used in their UDFs. There is a preference for clear documentation about reserved resources and usage limits within the software.
